## OpenWA self-chat bridge -- READ THIS FIRST

**What this workflow does, and no more:** receives OpenWA's `message.received` webhook,
keeps only events on Steven's own self-chat, and appends one JSON line per kept event to a
local queue file. It never replies, never calls OpenWA's send-message endpoint, and never
touches any client-facing system -- this is plumbing, not the answer.

**Why it stops there:** answering as Vanessa needs the AI team, the HALT list, and the §5a
marker / circuit-breaker state (`integrations/mac-task-specs.md` §5a) -- all of that runs in
the existing Claude-side inbox task, not in n8n. This workflow's only job is to get a
validated inbound event from OpenWA's webhook onto local disk reliably; the Mac task
(coordinated with lane C1) reads the queue file and does the rest, unchanged from §5a except
for which tool polls/pushes the raw message.

**Auth:** the Webhook node requires a Header Auth credential (`X-Webhook-Token`) that does
NOT ship with this file -- n8n credentials are never exported. Create one named exactly
`OpenWA webhook token` with header name `X-Webhook-Token` and the SAME value as
`OPENWA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` in `integrations/n8n/.env`, then also set that value as the `secret`
field when C1 registers this session's webhook on the OpenWA side (`POST
/api/sessions/{id}/webhooks`, see OpenWA's README "Setup Webhook"). Until that credential is
assigned, executing this workflow fails cleanly with a credentials-not-set error -- verified
in R9's sandbox test log.

**Before this queue file means anything:** `OPENWA_SELF_CHAT_ID` in the Code node below must
be set to the real self-chat `chatId` OpenWA reports for Steven's own number (lane C1 gets
this from the session once linked, the same way §5a's `chat find` step got it for
whatsapp-cli). Left as the placeholder, every event is filtered out -- safe by default, not
silently wrong.
